label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Indices, Surds & Quadratics

body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.

body.en:
Completing the square when \(a \neq 1\): Factor \(a\) from the quadratic and linear terms before halving the coefficient: \(ax^2+bx+c = a\left[x^2+\tfrac{b}{a}x\right]+c = a\left(x+\tfrac{b}{2a}\right)^2 - a\left(\tfrac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + c\). Forgetting to multiply the subtracted square by \(a\) is the most frequent algebraic slip.

Discriminant phrasing: 'Real roots' means \(b^2-4ac \ge 0\) (includes repeated roots). 'Two distinct real roots' strictly requires \(b^2-4ac > 0\). 'No real roots' means \(b^2-4ac < 0\). If the leading coefficient contains a parameter \(k\), remember \(k \neq 0\) for the equation to be quadratic.

Surd conjugates: To rationalise \(\frac{a}{b+\sqrt{c}}\), multiply numerator and denominator by \(b-\sqrt{c}\). Expanding \((b+\sqrt{c})(b-\sqrt{c}) = b^2 - c\) eliminates the radical completely.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Indices, Surds & Quadratics)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

question.en: Solve the quadratic equation \(2x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0\) by completing the square. State the vertex of the corresponding parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 5x - 3\).
question.ar: حل the quadratic equation \(2x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0\) by compليكنing the square. State the vertex of the corresponding parabola \(y = 2x^2 - 5x - 3\).

solution.en: Factor 2 from the first two terms: \(2\left(x^2 - \tfrac{5}{2}x\right) - 3 = 0\). Halve the coefficient of \(x\): \(\tfrac{1}{2}\left(-\tfrac{5}{2}\right) = -\tfrac{5}{4}\). Complete the square: \(2\left(x - \tfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 - 2\left(\tfrac{25}{16}\right) - 3 = 0\Rightarrow 2\left(x - \tfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 - \tfrac{25}{8} - \tfrac{24}{8} = 0\Rightarrow 2\left(x - \tfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \tfrac{49}{8}\). Divide by 2: \(\left(x - \tfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \tfrac{49}{16}\). Take square roots: \(x - \tfrac{5}{4} = \pm\tfrac{7}{4}\Rightarrow x = \tfrac{5+7}{4} = 3\) or \(x = \tfrac{5-7}{4} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\). The vertex is \(\left(\tfrac{5}{4}, -\tfrac{49}{8}\right) = (1.25, -6.125)\).

Compليكنe the square: \(2\left(x - \tfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 - 2\left(\tfrac{25}{16}\right) - 3 = 0\Rightarrow 2\left(x - \tfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 - \tfrac{25}{8} - \tfrac{24}{8} = 0\Rightarrow 2\left(x - \tfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \tfrac{49}{8}\). Divide by 2: \(\left(x - \tfrac{5}{4}\right)^2 = \tfrac{49}{16}\). Take square roots: \(x - \tfrac{5}{4} = \pm\tfrac{7}{4}\Rightarrow x = \tfrac{5+7}{4} = 3\) or \(x = \tfrac{5-7}{4} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\). The vertex is \(\left(\tfrac{5}{4}, -\tfrac{49}{8}\right) = (1.25, -6.125)\).

question.en: Express \(\dfrac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2-\sqrt{5}}\) in the form \(p + q\sqrt{5}\), where \(p\) and \(q\) are rational numbers to be found.
question.ar: Express \(\dfrac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2-\sqrt{5}}\) in the form \(p + q\sqrt{5}\), حيث \(p\) and \(q\) are rational numbers to be found.

solution.en: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, \(2+\sqrt{5}\): \[\dfrac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2-\sqrt{5}} \times \dfrac{2+\sqrt{5}}{2+\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{(3+\sqrt{5})(2+\sqrt{5})}{2^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2}\] Expanding the numerator: \(3(2) + 3\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5} + (\sqrt{5})^2 = 6 + 5\sqrt{5} + 5 = 11 + 5\sqrt{5}\). The denominator is \(4 - 5 = -1\). Therefore: \[\dfrac{11+5\sqrt{5}}{-1} = -11 - 5\sqrt{5}\] Thus \(p = -11\) and \(q = -5\).
solution.ar: Multiply numerator and denominator بتطبيق conjugate of the denominator, \(2+\sqrt{5}\): \[\dfrac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2-\sqrt{5}} \times \dfrac{2+\sqrt{5}}{2+\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{(3+\sqrt{5})(2+\sqrt{5})}{2^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2}\] فكّ المقدارing the numerator: \(3(2) + 3\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5} + (\sqrt{5})^2 = 6 + 5\sqrt{5} + 5 = 11 + 5\sqrt{5}\). The denominator is \(4 - 5 = -1\). Therefore: \[\dfrac{11+5\sqrt{5}}{-1} = -11 - 5\sqrt{5}\] Thus \(p = -11\) and \(q = -5\).

question.en: Find the set of values of the constant \(k\) for which the equation \(kx^2 + 4x + (k-3) = 0\) has real roots.
question.ar: أوجد set of values of the constant \(k\) for which the equation \(kx^2 + 4x + (k-3) = 0\) has real roots.

solution.en: For real roots, the discriminant \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac \ge 0\). Here \(a = k\), \(b = 4\), \(c = k-3\): \[\Delta = 4^2 - 4(k)(k-3) = 16 - 4k^2 + 12k \ge 0\] Divide the entire inequality by \(-4\), reversing the inequality sign: \[k^2 - 3k - 4 \le 0\] Factor the quadratic: \((k - 4)(k + 1) \le 0\). The critical values are \(k = -1\) and \(k = 4\). Since the parabola opens upward, the product is \(\le 0\) between the roots: \(-1 \le k \le 4\). Note that if \(k = 0\), the equation becomes the linear equation \(4x - 3 = 0\), which has one real root \(x = \tfrac{3}{4}\), so \(k = 0\) is included. Thus, the solution set is \(-1 \le k \le 4\).

The critical values are \(k = -1\) and \(k = 4\). Since the parabola opens upward, the product is \(\le 0\) between the roots: \(-1 \le k \le 4\). Note that إذا كان \(k = 0\), the equation becomes the linear equation \(4x - 3 = 0\), which has one real root \(x = \tfrac{3}{4}\), so \(k = 0\) is included. وعليه، the solution set is \(-1 \le k \le 4\).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Medium] Given the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0 \), find the sum of the roots.
question.ar: [Practice 5 · Medium] Given the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0 \), أوجد sum of the roots.

hints.en: For a quadratic equation in the form \( ax^2 + bx + c = 0 \), the sum of the roots is given by the formula \( -\frac{b}{a} \).
hints.ar: For a quadratic equation in the form \( ax^2 + bx + c = 0 \), the sum of the roots is given بتطبيق formula \( -\frac{b}{a} \).
